gen-righteous-gf-alumni-sans-pinstripe: Bent-steel curves that fill the line, all swagger and fun, set the tone in Righteous. And Alumni Sans Pinstripe, tight with oversized lowercase, wants extra size to hold its own.
gen-righteous-gf-carlito: Loud, ribbon-cut letters with real swagger. Righteous is built to announce, while Carlito, with its open round letters and tight spacing, is built to read clearly at small sizes.
gen-righteous-gf-farro: Loud bent-rod swagger from Righteous, with big bowls filling every line. Farro, compressed in its ascenders and free of any stroke contrast, keeps all that swagger grounded and approachable.
gen-righteous-gf-geist-mono: Bent-rod curves and big bowls make Righteous loud, while Geist Mono counters with fixed-width, code-style letters and high-rising lowercase. Showy next to structured, with fun leaning against technical rigor.
gen-righteous-gf-genos: Tight and smooth, the body text glides along without ever snagging on a closed-up bowl. Genos handles the quiet work with a modest weight gradient, while Righteous, compass-pencil consistent, does the shouting.
gen-righteous-gf-geom: Geom reads lofty and approachable, its lowercase standing tall. What makes the pair work is Righteous shouting in strokes of no contrast while Geom stays gently, modestly low in contrast.
gen-righteous-gf-jaldi: Approachable from the first line, Jaldi packs brushed letters tightly, its x-height pushed well above the usual. Righteous, with its neon-tube constancy, is for shouting; Jaldi is for reading.
gen-righteous-gf-mukta: Righteous bends thin steel rod into every letter. Mukta, clean with tall-bodied small letters, gives that showiness a quiet partner, and the loud-meets-quiet split is the pairing's best quality.
gen-righteous-gf-port-lligat-sans: Commanding and stencil-flat, Righteous holds one weight throughout. Port Lligat Sans then packs its characters like pins in a cushion, with a minimal cap-to-lowercase step, so the page moves from shout to murmur.
gen-righteous-gf-ramabhadra: Righteous brings loud, bent-rod bowls that fill every line. Ramabhadra, clean with a prominent x-height, sits comfortably under a heading whose t keeps crossbar and stem matched in weight.
